** ἀσχημ-ονέω**,
**behave unseemly, disgrace oneself,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 407, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 151, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 506d, etc.: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἀ. ἄλλα ἅ.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.53; ἀ. τὰ δεινότατα [prev. author] 60.25; μηδὲν ἀ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1273a34, compare “EN” 1119a30}}: with _participle_, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.178d:}} —_passive_, πολλὰ ἀσχημονεῖται many **unseemly things are done,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.26.}}

847:
** αὐτοῦ**,
_Doric dialect_ αὐτῶ and αὐτεῖ, _adverb_, properly _genitive_ of αὐτός:— **just there** or **just here,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.}}; ἐπίσχες αὐτοῦ stop **there!** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 66:}} —frequently with the place added, αὐτοῦ ἐνὶ Τροίῃ, μέν᾽ αὐτοῦ τῷδ᾽ ἐνὶ χώρῳ, **here in** Troy, etc., {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.237, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.271; αὐτοῦ ἔνθα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.207}}; που αὐτοῦ ἀγρῶν somewhere **there** on the farm, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.639; αὐτοῦ ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς 8.68; αὐτοῦ περὶ τεῖχος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 452 (Lyric poetry)}}; αὐτοῦ ταύτῃ in this **very** place, **exactly** here, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.214, 3.77, 4.135; αὐτοῦ τῇ περ ἔπεσε [prev. author] 1.30:}} — so that αὐτοῦ usually precedes; but κεῖθι αὐτοῦ{{Refs 6th c.BC+|“hymnus ad Apollinem” 374; κατ᾽ οἴκους αὐτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 89; ἐνθάδ᾽ αὐτοῦ 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 36.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1187; τοῖς ἐνθάδ᾽ αὐτοῦ μὴ κατ᾽ ἄστυ δημόταις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 78.}}

877:
** ἀφροσύνη**, ἡ,
(ἄφρων) **folly, thoughtlessness,** frequently in _plural_, παῖδας καταπαυέμεν ἀφροσυνάων{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.457, compare 16.278: in _sing._, οὐδέ τί σε χρὴ ταύτης ἀφροσύνης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.110, compare 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 254, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.146, 9.82; κοῦφαι ἀ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1230 (Lyric poetry); καταφρόνησιν ἢ.. ἀ. μετωνόμασται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.122}}; opposed to σωφροσύνη and σοφία, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 332e; συμβαίνει ἡ ἀ. μετὰ ἀκρασίας ἀρετή 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1146a27.}}

_Ionic dialect_ Ἀχαιΐη, ἡ, epithet of Demeter in Attica, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.61}}; also in Boeotia, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.378e}}; Ἀχέα at Thespiae, {{Refs|“IG” 7.1867}}.

896:
**Βάαλ** (Rec. βαάλ), ὁ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, **lord**),
**Baal**: Rom.11:4 (LXX). The fem. art. here agrees with the usage of LXX, where, following a similar Hebrew practice (בֹּשֶׁת for בַּעַל), αἰσχύνη appears to have been substituted in reading for the written Βάαλ (cf. 3Ki.18:19), and to account for the frequently use of the fem. art. bef. Β. The usage, however, is not general, and in the passage cited in Ro (3Ki.19:18), LXX reads τῷ Β. †
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
